Algebra I · Lesson 4.5

Word Problems

Solve this lesson →All lessons

4.4 closed with a promise, equations with no algebra written down at all, just plain English sentences. Here it is kept. A word problem states a fact about an unknown number, and chapter 4 already holds every move needed to find that number once the sentence becomes an equation. Try one cold.

Problem
A trail camera takes the same number of photos each night. After 6 nights, plus the 55 photos from the afternoon it was mounted, its card holds 553 photos. How many photos does it take each night?
Show a hint
  • Give the unknown a name in words first. Let nn be the number of photos taken each night, then reread the sentence with that name in it.
  • Six nights of nn photos plus the 5555 from the first afternoon makes 553553, so 6n+55=5536n+55=553.
Show the full solution
The six nights give 6n6n photos, so 6n+55=5536n+55=553. Subtract 5555, 6n=4986n=498, and divide by 66, n=83n=83​. Check against the story, 66 nights of 8383 photos is 498498, and the first afternoon's 5555 brings the card to 553553.

Look at what you just did. You named the unknown, photos per night. You turned the sentence into 6n+55=5536n+55=553, solved it with 4.2's moves, answered the question that was asked, and checked the value against the story. That is the entire method of this lesson, and you ran it before it had a name.

Key idea
The routine. Say what the variable stands for, units included. Translate the sentence into an equation. Solve with the chapter's moves. Answer the question that was asked. Then check against the story, not against your equation. That last part matters because the equation is only your translation of the sentence, and a mistranslation solved correctly will confirm itself perfectly, so the story is the only place a translation error can be caught.

The vocabulary translates a piece at a time. The sum of two quantities adds them, their difference subtracts them in the order named, and more than adds. Less than carries a trap. Seven less than nn means nn loses seven, so it is n−7n−7, not 7−n7−n. English names the subtracted amount first, and algebra writes it last.

Problem
Translate this sentence into an equation before solving anything. Eleven less than four times a number is 109109. Enter the number.
Show a hint
  • Decide which quantity gets subtracted before writing anything down. Eleven less than a thing means the thing loses eleven.
  • The equation is 4n−11=1094n−11=109, not 11−4n=10911−4n=109.
Show the full solution
Four times the number, less eleven, gives 4n−11=1094n−11=109. Add 1111, 4n=1204n=120, so n=30n=30​. The phrase names the eleven first, but the eleven is the amount taken away, so it is written last.
Problem
A novel and its sequel together run 584 pages, and the sequel is 68 pages longer than the novel. How many pages long is the sequel?
Show a hint
  • One letter can carry both books. Let it name the shorter one, and write the sequel's page count from it.
  • n+(n+68)=584n+(n+68)=584 gives the novel's pages. Reread the question before you type.
Show the full solution
Let nn be the novel's pages, so the sequel has n+68n+68 and n+(n+68)=584n+(n+68)=584. Then 2n+68=5842n+68=584, 2n=5162n=516, n=258n=258, and the sequel runs 258+68=326258+68=326​ pages. The solved letter answers only its own definition, the novel, so the last move is rereading the ask.
Key idea
Say what the variable stands for. Write its meaning down, units included, before any equation. When a story relates two quantities, let xx be the smaller and build the other from it, x+68x+68, three times xx, the total minus xx. A letter with no stated meaning cannot be checked against a story, and the solved value answers only its own definition, so answering the question that was asked is always a separate, final step.
Problem
A library cart holds 76 books, hardcovers and paperbacks, with three times as many paperbacks as hardcovers. How many hardcovers are on the cart?
Show a hint
  • Name the smaller count. The paperbacks are then written from it, not given a second letter.
  • Hardcovers plus three times hardcovers is 7676, so 4h=764h=76.
Show the full solution
Let hh be the hardcover count, so there are 3h3h paperbacks and h+3h=76h+3h=76. Then 4h=764h=76 and h=19h=19​. Check, 1919 hardcovers and 5757 paperbacks make 7676 books, and 5757 is three times 1919.

Runs of neighboring numbers translate through one variable too. Consecutive integers step by one, so three of them are xx, x+1x+1, x+2x+2. Consecutive even numbers step by two, skipping the odd number between, and consecutive odd numbers do the same, so either run is xx, x+2x+2, x+4x+4.

Problem
Three lockers in a row carry consecutive numbers, and the three numbers add to 222. Enter the largest of the locker numbers.
Show a hint
  • Let xx be the smallest locker number and write the other two from it.
  • The equation collects to 3x+3=2223x+3=222, and the answer is not xx.
Show the full solution
Let xx be the smallest, so x+(x+1)+(x+2)=222x+(x+1)+(x+2)=222. Then 3x+3=2223x+3=222, 3x=2193x=219, x=73x=73, and the largest is 73+2=7573+2=75​. Check, 73+74+75=22273+74+75=222.
Problem
House numbers on one side of a lane run through the odd numbers. Three neighbors' numbers add to 303. Enter the largest of the three.
Show a hint
  • Consecutive odd numbers are 22 apart, not 11 apart.
  • With xx the smallest, the equation collects to 3x+6=3033x+6=303, and the ask is the largest.
Show the full solution
Neighboring odd numbers step by 22, so the three are xx, x+2x+2, x+4x+4, and 3x+6=3033x+6=303. Then 3x=2973x=297, x=99x=99, and the largest is 103103​. One side of a street runs through every other number, which is why the step is 22.

Some stories state facts at two different moments. An age problem describes today, then jumps ahead, and a jump of six years adds six to every age in the story, both people, not just the one being asked about. Push every age forward, write the fact about the later moment, and the equation that falls out has the variable on both sides, 4.3's shape.

Problem
Mara is 39 years older than her daughter. In 7 years she will be exactly twice her daughter's age. How old is the daughter now, in years?
Show a hint
  • Write both ages now from one letter, then push both of them forward 77 years.
  • The equation is d+46=2(d+7)d+46=2(d+7), the 4.3 shape. Collect the variable terms.
Show the full solution
Let dd be the daughter's age now, so Mara is d+39d+39, and in 77 years d+39+7=2(d+7)d+39+7=2(d+7). Then d+46=2d+14d+46=2d+14, so d=32d=32​. Check against the story, in 77 years they are 3939 and 7878, and 7878 is twice 3939.
Problem
A cafe till holds 28 coins, every one a quarter or a dime, and together they are worth 5.05 dollars. How many of the coins are quarters?
Show a hint
  • One letter carries both counts. If qq of the coins are quarters, the other 28−q28−q are dimes.
  • Multiply the whole equation by 100100 the 4.4 way, so the hundredths become whole numbers.
Show the full solution
With qq quarters and 28−q28−q dimes, 0.25q+0.10(28−q)=5.050.25q+0.10(28−q)=5.05. Multiply by 100100, 25q+280−10q=50525q+280−10q=505, so 15q=22515q=225 and q=15q=15​. Check in the story, 1515 quarters are 3.753.75 dollars and 1313 dimes are 1.301.30, which is 5.055.05 in all.
Problem
A rectangular parade banner is 5 cm longer than it is wide, and its perimeter is 350 cm. How long is the banner, in centimeters?
Show a hint
  • Let ww be the width and write the length in terms of ww. The perimeter uses each of them twice.
  • 4w+10=3504w+10=350 gives the width. That is not what was asked.
Show the full solution
Let ww be the width, so the length is w+5w+5 and 2(w+w+5)=3502(w+w+5)=350. Then 4w+10=3504w+10=350, 4w=3404w=340, w=85w=85, and the length is 85+5=9085+5=90​ cm. Solving gives the width, but the question asks for the length, which is why rereading the question is part of the routine.

A wrong translation solved correctly passes every check against its own equation, because substituting a solution back into the equation it solves always works. The only check that reaches the translation is substituting into the English itself. That is 4.3's check-the-original rule pushed one step earlier, since here the original is the sentence.

Problem
A puzzle card reads, twelve less than six times a number is 138. Dev writes 12−6n=13812−6n=138, solves his own equation correctly, and gets n=−21n=−21, and a check in that equation passes. Check the story instead. Six times −21−21, then twelve less, gives −138−138, not 138138, so the translation is backwards. Fix it and enter the correct number.
Show a hint
  • Twelve less than six times nn starts from 6n6n and takes twelve away.
  • The correct equation is 6n−12=1386n−12=138.
Show the full solution
The correct translation is 6n−12=1386n−12=138, so 6n=1506n=150 and n=25n=25​. Dev's check passed because any correctly solved equation confirms itself. Only the story can catch the flip.
Fun fact
In twelfth-century India, Bhaskara II wrote the Lilavati, a mathematics book composed in Sanskrit verse, its problems posed as short stories addressed to a student. Word problems have carried algebra's teaching for centuries.
Problem
A carpenter saws off half of a board, then trims off another three quarters of a meter, and 4.5 meters remain. How long was the board, in meters?
Show a hint
  • Let xx be the board's full length in meters and write what each cut takes away from it.
  • Multiply x−x2−34=4.5x−2x​−43​=4.5 through by 44, the 4.4 move.
Show the full solution
Let xx be the full length, so x−x2−34=4.5x−2x​−43​=4.5. Multiply by 44, 4x−2x−3=184x−2x−3=18, so 2x=212x=21 and x=10.5x=10.5​ meters. Check in the story, half of 10.510.5 leaves 5.255.25, and trimming 0.750.75 more leaves 4.54.5.

An equation is a claim (4.1), balance moves solve it (4.2), on both sides (4.3), cleanup reaches the disguised ones (4.4). Translation feeds it anything plain English can say. Some stories name two quantities with no fact writing one from the other, so one letter stops being enough. Chapter 5 begins there, with 5.1 Two Variables, Two Equations.

Practice these ideas

Practice
The sum of a number and 97 is 189. Enter the number.
Show the solution
The sentence translates to n+97=189n+97=189. Subtract 9797 from both sides, so n=92n=92​. Check, 92+97=18992+97=189.
Practice
The difference of a number and 26 is 91. Enter the number.
Show the solution
n−26=91n−26=91. Add 2626 to both sides, so n=117n=117​. Check, 117−26=91117−26=91. The difference of aa and bb is a−ba−b, in the order named.
Practice
Eight more than seven times a number is 162. Enter the number.
Show the solution
7n+8=1627n+8=162. Subtract 88, so 7n=1547n=154, and divide by 77, so n=22n=22​. Check, 154+8=162154+8=162.
Practice
Nine less than six times a number is 219. Enter the number.
Show the solution
6n−9=2196n−9=219. Add 99, so 6n=2286n=228, and n=38n=38​. Check, 228−9=219228−9=219. English names the nine first, algebra writes it last.
Practice
A florist puts the same number of stems in each of 8 bouquets and has 17 stems left over, from 201 stems in all. How many stems are in each bouquet?
Show the solution
Let ss be the stems in each bouquet. Then 8s+17=2018s+17=201, so 8s=1848s=184 and s=23s=23​. Check, 8⋅23=1848⋅23=184, plus the 1717 left over is 201201.
Practice
A 102-meter rope is cut into two pieces, one 20 meters longer than the other. How long is the shorter piece, in meters?
Show the solution
Let the shorter piece be xx, so the longer is x+20x+20, and x+(x+20)=102x+(x+20)=102. Combine, 2x+20=1022x+20=102, so 2x=822x=82 and x=41x=41​. Check against the story, 41+61=10241+61=102 and 6161 is 2020 more than 4141.
Practice
A drama club has 152 members, with three times as many actors as crew members. How many actors does it have?
Show the solution
Let cc be the crew count, so there are 3c3c actors. Then c+3c=152c+3c=152, so 4c=1524c=152 and c=38c=38. The actors number 3⋅38=1143⋅38=114​. Check, 114+38=152114+38=152. The letter cc is the crew count, and the question asks for actors, so the final answer is 3c3c, not cc.
Practice
Two consecutive integers add to 141. Enter the smaller one.
Show the solution
x+(x+1)=141x+(x+1)=141, so 2x+1=1412x+1=141, 2x=1402x=140, and x=70x=70​. Check, 70+71=14170+71=141.
Practice
Three consecutive even integers add to 174. Enter the largest.
Show the solution
x+(x+2)+(x+4)=174x+(x+2)+(x+4)=174, so 3x+6=1743x+6=174, 3x=1683x=168, and x=56x=56. The largest is x+4=60x+4=60​. Check, 56+58+60=17456+58+60=174.
Practice
A rectangular parking lot is five times as long as it is wide, and its perimeter is 156 meters. How wide is the lot, in meters?
Show the solution
Let ww be the width in meters, so the length is 5w5w. The perimeter is 2(w+5w)=1562(w+5w)=156, so 12w=15612w=156 and w=13w=13​. Check, the length is 6565, and 2(13+65)=1562(13+65)=156.
Practice
A coach is 37 years older than his son. In 10 years he will be exactly twice as old as his son is then. How old is the son now, in years?
Show the solution
Let ss be the son's age now, so the coach is s+37s+37. In 10 years, s+47=2(s+10)s+47=2(s+10), so s+47=2s+20s+47=2s+20 and s=27s=27​. Check, in ten years they are 3737 and 7474, and 7474 is twice 3737.
Practice
Nine times a number is 136 more than five times the number. Enter the number.
Show the solution
9n=5n+1369n=5n+136. Subtract 5n5n, so 4n=1364n=136 and n=34n=34​. Check, 9⋅34=3069⋅34=306 and 5⋅34+136=3065⋅34+136=306.
Practice
Thirty-six less than half a number is 95. Enter the number.
Show the solution
n2−36=952n​−36=95. Add 3636, so n2=1312n​=131, and multiply by 22, so n=262n=262​. Check, half of 262262 is 131131, and 131−36=95131−36=95.
Practice
Fair ride tickets cost 2.50 dollars each, plus a flat 2.25 dollars for a wristband. Joon pays 84.75 dollars in all. How many tickets does he buy?
Show the solution
Let tt be the number of tickets. Then 2.50t+2.25=84.752.50t+2.25=84.75. Multiply by 100100, 250t+225=8475250t+225=8475, so 250t=8250250t=8250 and t=33t=33​. Check, 3333 tickets cost 82.5082.50 dollars, plus 2.252.25 is 84.7584.75.
Practice
Aquarium tickets cost 5.50 dollars for adults and 4.25 dollars for students. A group of 35 people pays 185 dollars in all. How many adults are in the group?
Show the solution
Let aa be the adults, so 35−a35−a are students. Then 5.50a+4.25(35−a)=1855.50a+4.25(35−a)=185. Multiply by 100100, 550a+425(35−a)=18500550a+425(35−a)=18500, so 550a+14875−425a=18500550a+14875−425a=18500, 125a=3625125a=3625, and a=29a=29​. Check, 2929 adults pay 159.50159.50 dollars, 66 students pay 25.5025.50, and the total is 185185.
Practice
Three years from now, Ada will be four times as old as she was three years ago. How old is Ada now, in years?
Show the solution
Let nn be Ada's age now. Then n+3=4(n−3)n+3=4(n−3), so n+3=4n−12n+3=4n−12, 15=3n15=3n, and n=5n=5​. Check, in three years she is 88, three years ago she was 22, and 88 is four times 22.
Practice
A worksheet reads, eighteen less than nine times a number is 198. Kai writes 18−9n=19818−9n=198, solves it correctly, and gets n=−20n=−20, and a check in his own equation passes. The story check fails, since nine times −20−20, then eighteen less, is −198−198. Fix the translation and enter the correct number.
Show the solution
9n−18=1989n−18=198. Add 1818, so 9n=2169n=216 and n=24n=24​. Check, 9⋅24=2169⋅24=216, and eighteen less is 198198. Kai's check passed because a correctly solved equation always confirms itself, and only the story catches the flip.
Practice
Twice the sum of a number and 71 is 104 less than four times the number. Enter the number.
Show the solution
2(n+71)=4n−1042(n+71)=4n−104. Distribute, 2n+142=4n−1042n+142=4n−104. Subtract 2n2n, then add 104104, so 246=2n246=2n and n=123n=123​. Check, twice the sum is 2⋅194=3882⋅194=388, and 4⋅123−104=3884⋅123−104=388.
